lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.criterion: Identity binding — same-name Text Signal scope
findings.observation: Confirmed defect: the frozen product can offer two active, confirmed candidate roles for different People with the same display name in one Pursuit, but the Text Signal picker renders each option only as personDisplayLabel plus pursuitTitle. The selected readback adds milestone, revision, and role type, none of which distinguishes those two People. The recruiter therefore cannot make a meaningful identity choice before exact evidence is bound to one Person.
findings.evidence: Frozen source manifest sha256 071897e3687eaf955f7198db29f186b86371dd97fbbd911441f4cd6b5f4061e9: apps/backend/src/evaluation/runPursuitEvidenceIntegrityEvaluation.ts:150-188 creates two distinct People both named Alex Chen and :211-243 places both as active confirmed candidate roles in the same Pursuit; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-07/pursuit-evidence-integrity-runtime.json records both Person IDs. apps/ios/Sources/Services/TextSignalSyncClient.swift:183-207 creates one scope per role and retains relationship context, while apps/ios/Sources/Features/TextSignalCaptureView.swift:169-191 omits that context and all stable identity clues from both the picker label and selected-scope readback. No frozen UI test covers this same-name Text Signal path.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can attach private candidate words, attribution, and a downstream milestone Proposal to the wrong same-name candidate while believing they completed an explicit identity review, contaminating the candidate record and risking an inappropriate follow-up.
findings.recommendation: Make every Person choice meaningfully distinguishable with a stable, recruiter-recognizable clue tied to the selected active role, such as the relevant relationship context plus a verified source or contact clue; never use an unrelated first context. Require the client and server to verify that the chosen workspace, Pursuit, role, Person, and relationship context are mutually consistent before capture persistence, and preserve that exact binding in the review receipt.
findings.verification: Seed one Pursuit with two active confirmed candidate roles whose People share the same display name but have distinct verified contexts. In Text Signal, neither option is preselected, each option and VoiceOver label is uniquely understandable, swapping any role/Person/context identifier is rejected, and a completed sync reads back the intended Person ID, role ID, context ID, capture ID, and evidence fragment ID. Repeat after relaunch and offline recovery.

findings.criterion: State integrity — success receipt belongs to the submitted operation
findings.observation: Confirmed validation defect with bounded production evidence: response-loss and relaunch now remain unknown until canonical readback, but the iOS trusted-readback predicate does not bind the receipt to the operation it just persisted and does not require canonical_applied outcome or applied Proposal status. A frozen unit test reaches recorded success even though its generated operation UUID cannot equal the hard-coded receipt operation ID.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Sources/Features/PursuitProposalReviewStore.swift:190-205 creates a fresh operation ID, but :265-274 validates only Proposal ID, Pursuit ID, revisions, and empty effects; reconciliation at :227-241 likewise does not compare readback.operation.id and receipt.operationID. apps/ios/Tests/PursuitProposalReviewStoreTests.swift:14-38 accepts recorded success using the receipt hard-coded at :235-244, and :68-82 plus :97-120 accept the same unrelated receipt during reconciliation. In contrast, docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-04/ios-canonical-review-runtime.json and docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-08/p0-journey-runtime.json directly prove the frozen honest-backend response-loss journey locks, reconciles, performs one POST, and agrees with PostgreSQL; therefore the prior false-success defect is removed for that tested journey, not for malformed or mis-associated readbacks.
findings.user_impact: A malformed, stale, or mis-associated response that happens to carry matching entity revisions can unlock the success receipt for the wrong operation. That weakens the very canonical readback boundary meant to prevent the recruiter from acting on a false success.
findings.recommendation: Pass the expected operation ID into the trusted-readback check and require operation.id, receipt.operationID, proposal.id and status, Pursuit ID, canonical_applied outcome, exact before/after revision transition, actor/workspace scope, decisions, changed fields, and zero external effects to agree. Any mismatch must remain unknownLocked and preserve the pending operation for reconciliation.
findings.verification: Add fake-service tests for a wrong receipt operation ID, wrong operation ID, non-applied Proposal, non-canonical outcome, wrong actor/workspace, unexpected changed field, and inconsistent revision transition; every case remains unknownLocked and never renders Canonical Pursuit updated. Re-run the response-loss relaunch journey and prove exactly one POST plus one matching database operation and receipt.

findings.criterion: Deletion and temporal truth — already applied evidence-backed fields
findings.observation: Credible risk inferred from frozen source: source deletion truthfully supersedes open Proposals and degrades role and gap evidence authority, but already applied Pursuit Proposals are excluded from deletion supersession and the canonical milestone remains a bare scalar without evidence state or recruiter-attribution metadata. The frozen deletion evaluator deletes only before review, so it does not prove how an applied evidence-backed milestone is represented after its governing source is deleted.
findings.evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/captures.ts:1142-1167 supersedes only needs_review, confirming, conflict, and failed Pursuit Proposals; applied is omitted. apps/backend/src/modules/pursuits.ts:462-493 returns milestone without the basis/evidence_state projected for roles. apps/ios/Sources/Domain/PursuitWorkspace.swift:134-143 models the milestone as a plain string, and apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:453-458, :527-547, and :785-792 display it without source-deleted or recruiter-confirmed lineage. apps/backend/src/evaluation/runPursuitEvidenceIntegrityEvaluation.ts:283-358 stages then deletes an unreviewed Proposal; docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-04/pursuit-proposal-runtime.json explicitly lists source-deletion retraction of an already applied Pursuit field as missing proof.
findings.user_impact: After a privacy deletion, a recruiter may continue to see and act on a milestone that looks current without being able to tell whether it remains an explicit recruiter decision, lost its supporting evidence, or should be reconsidered. This can silently sever source and temporal authority even when deletion of the raw content is correct.
findings.recommendation: Define the post-deletion semantic explicitly. If the human decision remains authoritative, project the field as recruiter-confirmed with actor, time, receipt, and source-unavailable status; if evidence is required, retract or contest it. Add field-level provenance for milestone and preserve privacy-safe deletion lineage without retaining deleted content.
findings.verification: Apply an evidence-supported milestone, verify its receipt, delete the only source, and read the Pursuit through backend and iOS after relaunch. The raw source is gone, the applied decision and deletion lineage remain inspectable, and every Today/detail surface either marks the field source unavailable with human decision attribution or retracts/contests it according to the declared policy. Retry deletion and prove the result is idempotent.

findings.criterion: Provenance — field-level replay and confirmation history
findings.observation: Credible risk: the Proposal review shows exact evidence text, source name, channel, observed time, speaker, attribution, review status, and inference labeling, which is materially stronger than a generic summary. The frozen iOS review evidence does not, however, prove a recruiter can replay the full field-level chain to the fragment/asset locator, parser version, edit history, confirmer and confirmation time, or superseding event; screenshot/OCR-specific bounding box, language, and recognition confidence are also not demonstrated.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-05/ios-canonical-proposal-review.png shows exact quote and review metadata but no source asset or fragment locator, parser/version, edit/confirmation history, or supersession control. docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-prd-07/pursuit-evidence-integrity-runtime.json carries fragment_id, parser name/version, source timezone, and review state in backend review_context, demonstrating partial backend provenance rather than end-to-end iOS replay. The final artifact provides no frozen screenshot/OCR field replay case.
findings.user_impact: When a candidate disputes wording or a recruiter audits a corrected extraction, the reviewer may be unable to determine from the product surface exactly which source region, transformation version, edit, and human confirmation produced the field.
findings.recommendation: Add a privacy-safe provenance drill-down from every material Proposal field to its immutable fragment and authorized source asset, including source region when applicable, parser/model/policy version, edits, confirmer, timestamps, and supersession/deletion state. Keep generated interpretation visually separate from observed content.
findings.verification: Using synthetic screenshot, typed-text, and audio-derived fixtures, replay each proposed field from the review UI to the exact governed fragment and source region, inspect version/edit/confirmer history, then correct and supersede it. The old interpretation remains audit-visible, deleted content remains unavailable, and no generated text is relabeled as evidence.

strengths: The tested false-success journey is genuinely improved: submit persists an idempotent operation, ambiguous response loss enters unknownLocked, relaunch reconciles without resubmission, success appears only after the tested canonical Pursuit/receipt readback, and the database oracle records one operation with zero external effects.

Backend Proposal staging and review revalidate account scope, active authorized evidence, reviewed attribution, identity binding, active Pursuit role membership, exact decisions, base revision, and idempotency under row locks before one canonical internal mutation.

Typed Signal keeps exact text local before explicit sync, uses protected atomic storage, preserves the same ID across interruption/retry, and removes the local payload only after a matching canonical deletion receipt.

Deletion propagation is broad for governed source content and derivatives: it redacts evidence and source fields, revokes pending approvals, supersedes open Proposals, degrades role/gap authority, preserves structured lineage, and is account-scoped and idempotent in the synthetic evaluator.

The deterministic Agent control plane exposes only read_pursuit, read_evidence, stage_pursuit_proposal, and record_no_action; 30 frozen trials cover supported action, no_action, prompt injection, malformed output, token exhaustion, and deletion-after-snapshot with zero external effects and quarantined unsafe output.
The frozen source and tests prohibit person ranking and candidate quality, fit, personality, protected-trait, or acceptance-probability inference in the reviewed slice.
missing_evidence: Five credentialed live Claude Agent SDK trials against the frozen evaluator and any live-model stability or tool-boundary evidence; status is correctly not_run_missing_credentials and live release remains missing_proof.

Production authentication, production cross-tenant adversarial testing, regional controls, retention jobs, backup/cache/analytics/vendor deletion, export, monitoring, and model/vendor training-default evidence.
Any production external-provider write, permission-change, reconciliation, reversal, or provider-result proof; the frozen slice intentionally proves zero external effects only.
A frozen end-to-end same-name Text Signal UI fixture with two same-name active roles in one Pursuit and an identity-binding database oracle.
A frozen post-apply source-deletion journey for an evidence-supported Pursuit field.
End-to-end screenshot/OCR replay with source region, language, recognition confidence, transformation version, edit history, confirmer, and supersession evidence.

Physical-device capture and Data Protection verification, manual VoiceOver traversal, authorized real-candidate or candidate-side evidence, and design-partner field comparison; real candidate data must remain excluded from this panel.
Evaluator calibration against a human-reviewed gold set, blinded author/model identity, repeated order swaps, disagreement stability, and drift monitoring.
vetoes: Same-name Text Signal scope choices are visually indistinguishable, so exact evidence can be bound to the wrong Person despite a nominal picker review.
open_questions: Which recruiter-recognizable, purpose-appropriate identity clues are guaranteed for two same-name People in the same Pursuit, and how will the selected role be tied to the relevant rather than first relationship context?

After an evidence-backed milestone is applied and its sole source is deleted, is the milestone intended to persist as an explicitly recruiter-authored decision, become contested, or be retracted, and where will that temporal authority be visible?
Will the production review service make operation, receipt, actor, workspace, outcome, decisions, and changed-field concordance independently verifiable by the client?
What are the production retention and deletion guarantees for backups, logs, analytics, caches, embeddings, evaluation artifacts, and model/provider systems?
